name: Word Caption Clip
summary: A talking head in a vertical frame, with the speech shown as huge captions, one to three words at a time. Each word pops in at the beat, and the current word takes a bright colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: Make every word visible at the moment it is spoken: the caption is the main picture, and the viewer reads and hears the same beat.
design_principles: Set captions at 72px to 110px on a 1080x1920 frame, with 1 to 3 words on screen at a time.
Place the caption block at 55% to 65% of the frame height, centred, inside a 64px safe margin.
Colour the spoken word in yellow (#FFE600) or green (#3DFF7A) and keep the other words white.
Add a 6px black outline or a 4px hard shadow to each word.
Pop each word in at 90% to 110% scale over 6 to 8 frames at 30 fps.
Time each word to the audio within 2 frames.
Use a bold, heavy sans in capitals and one emoji or icon per sentence at most.
anti_patterns: Full sentences of 12 words on screen
Captions in the lower 15% of the frame, under the app buttons
Subtitles that lag the voice by more than 4 frames
Many colours in one caption line

layout.grid_mechanics: A 1080x1920 frame: the speaker fills the frame, and the caption block sits on a centred column of 880px at 55% to 65% of the height.
layout.whitespace_ratio: The caption block uses 15% of the frame; the speaker keeps the rest.
layout.alignment_rules: Captions centre on one axis; one to three words per line; line gap of 8px; no text under the platform buttons.
layout.container_geometry: No boxes: text with an outline or a 4px hard shadow; an optional pill of 999px behind one key word.

font_pairings.note: Heavy Montserrat (900) is an open look-alike of the black sans that word captions use.
Anton is an open look-alike of the Impact face for tall, narrow words.
A heavy geometric face with a round, clean text face.

typography.tracking: Display takes 0em; stacked lines stay tight at 0.
hierarchy_rules: Use one display weight (900) for all caption words.
Use sizes 72, 96 and 110px in the frame and 18px on a page.
Set the active word in the accent colour and all other words in white.
Set a small emoji at 64px beside the key word.

color.palette_structure: White words on any footage, one yellow or green active colour and a black outline.
color.contrast_rules: White words on frame black hold at least 19:1, and the 6px outline keeps them readable on any footage.
color.surface_treatment: Flat colour only; the speaker's footage is the picture, and a 20% black layer under the words lifts the contrast on a bright scene.
color.light_and_shadow: A hard 4px black shadow at 100% under each word; no glow and no blur.

materiality.surface_simulation: A phone video with live text on top: sharp, flat vector letters over camera footage.
materiality.border_rules: A 6px black outline on the words; no panel borders.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: No blur; a 4px hard offset shadow gives lift.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Solid emoji and icons at 64px beside the key word; thick, round shapes.
ornamentation_details.illustration: The speaker and the words; a progress bar of 6px at the top for long clips.

motion.transition_physics: Each word pops from 90% to 110% to 100% scale over 6 to 8 frames at 30 fps; the active colour moves from word to word on the beat; there is no fade between words.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover raises a card by 2px and shows a 4px yellow edge; active state fills the text with yellow.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels pulled along by the voice and cannot look away from the words.

avoid_when: The caption block would cover key footage.
The tone needs a quiet, cinematic mood.

modifiers.how: Move to sentence subtitles at 36px, a serif face and a muted grade.
Add a face cut-out, a red arrow and a 120px headline at the frame top.
Replace the speaker with an avatar and use pastel words with a plum outline.

pack.why: A heavy, solid family matches the thick caption letters and the emoji accents.

ground.why: The ground is raw footage with no decoration, since the words are the only design layer.
